text: Beyond Python's built-in errors, you can define your own exception types for your program's specific problems.
A custom exception is just a class that inherits from Exception.
Here InsufficientFunds stores extra details — how much was needed and how much was available.
[chuckle] It calls super with a clear message, so it prints nicely like any built-in error.
[sniff] Your code raises it exactly when the specific bad situation happens, with the relevant data attached.
So withdraw refuses to overdraw the account, raising the custom error with the exact numbers.
[sigh] The handler catches your specific type, ignoring unrelated errors, and reads the attached details.
We can even compute how far short the withdrawal was, using the data the exception carried along.
[groan] Custom exceptions make your error handling precise and self-documenting — callers know exactly what went wrong.
